After eight months in the MASc program, outstanding students are offered the opportunity to transfer directly to the PhD program. Should they accept this opportunity, the transfer would take effect after twelve months in the MASc program. Following the transfer, the student would have four years of guaranteed funding in the PhD program for a combined total of five years of funding in the MASc and PhD programs..
MASc Degree
What are the program fees?
For the MASc program, the program fees are covered by the financial support package provided by the supervisor for a limited period. Tuition fee amounts can be found on Student Accounts.
What is the minimum average required for admission to the MASc program?
To qualify for admission to the MASc programs, you require a mid-B average at the undergraduate level in the final year of study. In general, students admitted to the MASc program have an undergraduate average considerably higher than this. If you hold credentials outside of Canada, please review International Credentials Equivalencies to see if you meet the minimum requirements.
What is the difference between the SGS Fee Payment Deadline and the UTIAS Application System Deadline?

Is there funding available for the PhD program? How does the funding work?
Yes, all research programs are funded, including tuition, fees and a stipend for living expenses.
For the PhD program, students are guaranteed four years of funding for the first four years in the PhD program. Support is paid three times per year in September, January and May.
The funding is sufficient to pay tuition and fees, either domestic or international, and also includes a stipend to support living expenses. This funding is provided by the professor supervising the student’s research and is usually connected to a particular funded research project being undertaken by the professor.
How should I monitor the progress of my application?
Applicants should monitor their application on the UTIAS Application System. A completed application will have an Application Status of “application received”.
An application will remain as “application received” while it is under review. For many applicants the application status will continue to read “application received” until an admission decision has been made.
When are applications reviewed?

It is the applicant’s responsibility to communicate with their referees to ensure timely submission of letters of reference;
Applications missing any document (including letters of reference or English Proficiency test scores) will be deemed incomplete, and will not be assessed by the admissions committee;

Switzerland is a very expensive country, but the tuition fees are relatively low compared to e.g. the USA or UK. You have to pay the tuition fees and contributions at the University of Zurich (UZH). Regarding the costs of living in Switzerland, UZH maintains a website with guidelines: https://www.uzh.ch/en/studies/planning/finances.html
ETH Zurich maintains its own website: https://www.ethz.ch/en/the-eth-zurich/welcome-center/services-and-downloads/cost-of-living.html
The expected minimum costs of living are around 2200-2500 CHF per month (including tuition fees), but depend very much on the individual student. Especially the costs of housing are very variable.

When you book your interview, you will receive information about the interview process, and your obligations. These include ensuring you are in a private location, not communicating in any way with another person during the interview and not taking or accessing any form of notes (physical or electronic) during the interview.  Additionally, you will not be permitted to use generative Artificial Intelligence tools for any aspect of the interview process.
